title: Adding server D moves only the keys on D's new arc
caption: D lands at 65 and takes over the arc (50, 65] from C. Every other key keeps its owner.

steps.text: D hashes to 65, between B (50) and C (85). Nothing else on the ring moves.
Keys at 58 and 63 now meet D before C. They are the only keys that change owner: copy or re-warm just these.
Key 74 is past D, so it still walks on to C.
A and B, and the keys they own, are untouched: 2 of 8 keys moved, against 5 of 8 with hash % N.

scenarios.name: New node starts cold
scenarios.summary: D owns its keys the moment it joins but holds none of their data: every read on its arc misses until it warms up.

steps.text: D joins and the clients' rings update: keys at 58 and 63 now route to D.
D's cache is empty, so each of those reads misses and goes to the database.
C still holds those keys but nobody asks it any more: wasted memory until they're evicted.
Fix: copy the arc from C before D takes traffic, or on a miss let D read from the old owner first. Add nodes before the peak, not during it.

scenarios.name: Risk: adds little capacity
scenarios.summary: One random point means D relieves only the one server whose arc it splits, and by a random amount. Virtual nodes let a new server take a small slice from everyone.

steps.text: D lands at a hashed position: here between B and C, so only C gives up keys.
A and B, even if they are the hot ones, get no relief at all.
Had D landed at 52, it would take almost nothing. With 100+ vnodes it takes about 1/N of the ring, a little from every server.
